concept.title: Rate Volatility + Equity Selloff = Flight to Quality
concept.one_liner: Rising long-end yields (10Y +5bps) amid equity weakness (-1.91%) signals repricing of growth and Fed path
concept.explanation: The S&P 500 declined 1.91% while 10Y Treasury yields rose 5 basis points, a classic bearish steepening pattern. This suggests investors are simultaneously reducing equity exposure and demanding higher yields on safe-haven bonds. The uptick in VIX to 19.30 and mixed messaging on mega-cap tech (Nvidia caution vs. J&J strength) indicate selective de-risking rather than broad panic, but the direction is toward defensive repositioning ahead of Friday's FOMC press release.
concept.market_link: With FOMC communication Friday and crude stabilizing around $89.62, the narrative hinges on whether the Fed signals cuts or holds—a decision that will either validate the equity selloff or trigger a relief rally

narrative: U.S. equities fell 1.91% to 7400 as long-end Treasury yields rose 5bps to 5.15%, signaling a tactical shift toward safety and re-pricing of Fed policy expectations ahead of Friday's FOMC press release. Oil stabilization and mixed sector momentum (Lilly diversification, Nvidia skepticism) suggest rotational weakness rather than systemic capitulation, but elevated VIX (19.30) reflects genuine near-term uncertainty.
